page: Microsoft Azure HB368-192rs_v5 is a high-performance computing instance within the HBv5 series, built for compute-intensive parallel simulations and modeling tasks. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the server delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs. It features 448.0 GB of system memory, equating to 2.33 GB of RAM per core, emphasizing processing concurrency over large per-thread memory allocations.

Data storage and interconnect capabilities are centered around high-throughput demands. The server incorporates 15875 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, offering extensive high-speed scratch capacity on the host. Network communication features Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) support alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage, supporting low-latency node clustering. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default.

The hardware configuration provides high physical resource density and throughput efficiency for large scale-out clusters. The tradeoff is a lean memory-to-core ratio, which is less suited for massive in-memory databases but optimal for compute pipelines where data can be staged locally. The instance fits workloads such as computational fluid dynamics, weather forecasting, finite element analysis, molecular dynamics, and large-scale parallel batch processing.
description: Microsoft Azure HB368-192rs_v5 is a high-performance computing instance from the HBv5 family, designed for compute-heavy parallel workloads. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V with x86_64 Intel processors, the instance delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs and 448.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.33 GB per core. The server includes 15875 GB of local NVMe SSD storage to handle intensive temporary disk operations, complemented by RDMA capability for low-latency inter-node communication and Premium Storage support. It operates without discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dense core count and large local NVMe volume provide efficient execution for distributed scientific pipelines, while the moderate memory-per-core ratio prioritizes raw compute capacity over large monolithic in-memory datasets. Workloads suited for this server include computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, molecular modeling, and multi-node scientific simulations requiring high-speed local scratch disks.
